page: Amazon Web Services i2.4xlarge is a storage-optimized, second-generation instance type utilizing the Xen hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor with 16 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz and includes a 25 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 122.0 GB of system memory, providing 7.62 GB per core, and includes 3200 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Network connectivity is established with a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place the i2.4xlarge in the average tier for most compute and memory operations. The instance achieves a PassMark CPU score of 16,683.51 and a single-core Geekbench score of 532.0, indicating lower single-threaded efficiency. However, multi-core stress-ng CPU performance reaches 14,125.68, and PassMark database operations score 6,516.2, both falling within the average category. Memory bandwidth tests show a strong read-only small block cached speed of 588.91 GB/sec, though large block write speeds are weaker at 18.74 GB/sec. Redis SET operations perform at an average rate of 6.04 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput reaches 14.27 GB/sec.

The hardware profile of the i2.4xlarge presents clear tradeoffs. While it offers high-capacity local NVMe SSD storage and a substantial memory footprint, its older Intel Xeon architecture lacks advanced instruction sets like AVX-512, AMX, or SHA extensions, resulting in weaker performance for modern workloads such as LLM inference and single-threaded decompression. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance is suited for legacy database systems, caching layers, and storage-intensive applications that require high local storage density and moderate compute power without the premium cost of current-generation architectures.
description: Amazon Web Services i2.4xlarge is a storage-optimized, second-generation instance featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs on an Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor running at 2.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture with the Xen hypervisor, it includes 122.0 GB of memory and 3200 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The instance delivers average performance across database operations, with a PassMark database score of 6,516.2 and Redis SET throughput of 6.04 million operations per second. However, its older CPU architecture lacks modern instruction sets like AVX-512, leading to weaker single-core and decompression benchmarks. With a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses, the i2.4xlarge represents a balanced option for storage-intensive workloads, legacy databases, and caching systems requiring high local storage capacity and moderate compute density.
